cards.name: Color Control
cards.summary: An expression control that holds one colour value and draws nothing by itself. Other properties read it through expressions, so one swatch can recolour a whole template.
use_for: one brand/party colour driving every lower-third bar, outline and highlight in a news template
recolouring an explainer infographic per channel from a single control
exposing a colour choice in an Essential Graphics template (MOGRT) for Premiere editors
avoid: expecting it to change the picture: without an expression linking to it nothing happens
pick-whipping many layers to a control on a layer that later gets renamed or deleted breaks every expression

params.name: Color
params.does: the colour value that expressions read, as [r, g, b, a] in 0-1
params.typical: brand hex, e.g. #FF6A00 saffron or #0A2A66 navy

cards.scripting: Status needs_input because it renders nothing until another property's expression references it. Put it on a null or a guide 'CONTROLS' layer, rename the effect (e.g. 'Brand Color') and read it with thisComp.layer("CONTROLS").effect("Brand Color")("Color"). The value is [r, g, b, a] in 0-1. Premiere has no expression controls; the closest is a colour parameter exposed in an Essential Graphics MOGRT.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Dropdown Menu Control
cards.summary: An expression control that holds a menu choice (a 1-based index) and draws nothing by itself. Expressions read the index to switch layouts, colours or text in a template.
use_for: one menu that switches a lower-third between party colour themes or layouts
picking left/centre/right alignment or a 9:16 vs 16:9 layout in a reusable explainer template
exposing a style choice in a MOGRT for Premiere editors
avoid: forgetting that the value is an index, not the item text
changing the menu items by script invalidates the old effect/property references

params.name: Menu
params.does: the selected item as a 1-based index
params.typical: 1-3 with the default three items; up to the number of items set by script

cards.scripting: Status needs_input: nothing renders until an expression reads it. Default items are Item 1/2/3 (harvest max = 3). Rename items with menuProp.setPropertyParameters(["Saffron", "Navy", "Green"]) (AE 17.0.1+); it returns the updated Menu property and invalidates old references, so use the returned property (or fetch the effect again) before setting values. AdobeBridge specs clamp Menu to the harvested max 3, so when a script adds more items, set the index with ExtendScript (menuProp.setValue(n)). Read in expressions as effect("Dropdown Menu Control")("Menu").value (1-based), typically inside a switch or array lookup.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Layer Control
cards.summary: An expression control that points at another layer in the comp and draws nothing by itself. Expressions use it to read that layer's position, opacity or other properties without hard-coding its name.
use_for: a callout arrow or name tag that follows whichever leader photo or null the editor picks
switching which tracked null a label, blur box or highlight follows in a news template
rigs that copy another layer's opacity or position without depending on layer names
avoid: leaving it at None: expressions that read it then error
expecting it to reach a layer in another comp: it only lists layers of its own comp (use comp("Name").layer("X") in the expression instead)

params.name: Layer
params.does: which layer of the same comp the control references
params.typical: index of a null, photo or tracked layer

cards.scripting: Layer is a layer-type property: AdobeBridge specs cannot set it. Use ExtendScript: eff.property("Layer").setValue(targetLayer.index) (0 = None). In an expression effect("Layer Control")("Layer") returns the Layer object, e.g. effect("Layer Control")("Layer").transform.position. Status needs_input: renders nothing on its own.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Point Control
cards.summary: An expression control that holds one x,y position (with an on-screen handle) and draws nothing by itself. Expressions read it to place pointers, line ends or effect centres from one draggable point.
use_for: end point of a callout leader line pointing at a person or object in a press photo
one draggable centre shared by a zoom, blur and spotlight in an explainer
receiving motion-tracker data so labels and highlights follow a moving subject
map pin or route end point in a political/news map graphic
avoid: mixing up layer space and comp space when the control sits on a scaled or moved layer

params.name: Point
params.does: the x,y position expressions read
params.typical: [960, 540] centre; any pixel point of the 1920x1080 comp

cards.scripting: 2d_spatial with no range: pixels in the space of the layer it sits on (equals comp space on an untransformed full-frame null). Convert with toComp()/fromComp() in expressions if the layer is moved or scaled. The tracker can apply track points to it (Edit Target > Effect Point Control). Status needs_input: renders nothing on its own.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: Slider Control
cards.summary: An expression control that holds one keyframeable number and draws nothing by itself. It is the standard way to drive counting numbers, progress bars and master intensity knobs.
use_for: animated counting numbers in stat cards (vote counts, seats won, budget figures) via a Source Text expression
progress bar or percentage fill in an explainer chart
one master intensity knob for wiggle/camera-shake amount across many layers
exposing a numeric parameter in a MOGRT for Premiere editors
avoid: showing raw decimals: wrap the value in Math.round() or toFixed()
values beyond plus/minus 1,000,000 are clamped, so big rupee figures need scaling (slider in lakh/crore units, multiply in the expression)

params.name: Slider
params.does: the number expressions read (UI slider shows 0-100 but accepts the full range)
params.typical: 0-100 for percentages; up to 1,000,000 for counts

cards.scripting: Harvested range -1,000,000 to 1,000,000; spec values outside are clamped. Counter: on a text layer's Source Text, Math.round(effect("Slider Control")("Slider")). Use easy-ease keyframes on the slider so the count decelerates. Status needs_input: renders nothing until an expression reads it.

verified.note: status needs_input: renders nothing on its own, so no frame was made

cards.name: 4-Color Gradient
cards.summary: Generates a smooth gradient blended from four coloured points. With Blending Mode None (default) it replaces the layer as a gradient plate and Opacity only fades it towards transparency; with Normal (or another mode) it lays a colour wash over the footage.
use_for: slowly moving soft-gradient background for explainer title cards and AI-channel graphics
colour wash over archival or b-roll to unify a sequence's palette
brand-coloured backdrop behind cut-out leader photos in news reels
background for quote cards and text-only reel slides
avoid: Blending Mode 1 (None) drops the footage at any Opacity: Opacity 60 only gives a dimmed, translucent gradient (dark over an empty comp), not a wash
the saturated rainbow defaults look cheap; pick 2-3 related hues
high Jitter adds noise that turns blocky after Instagram/YouTube compression

params.name: Point 1
params.does: position of colour 1 in comp pixels (Points 2-4 work the same)
params.typical: [192, 108] top-left default; move inward to tighten the blend

params.name: Color 1
params.does: colour at Point 1 (Colors 2-4 likewise)
params.typical: brand hues, e.g. #FF6A00, #FFD400, #00A3FF, #7A00FF

params.name: Blend
params.does: how softly the four colours mix; higher = smoother transitions

params.name: Jitter
params.does: noise added to break up gradient banding

params.name: Opacity
params.does: strength of the gradient over the original layer
params.typical: 30-60 with Blending Mode 2 (Normal) for a wash over footage; 100 with None for a background plate

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: 1-based popup: how the gradient combines with the layer
params.typical: 1 (None: gradient replaces the layer) for plates; 2 (Normal: gradient over the footage at Opacity) for washes

cards.scripting: Points are comp pixels; defaults sit at 10%/90% of 1920x1080. Property names are flat ('Point 1', 'Color 1' ...); the second 'Color 4' header in the harvest is only the group end marker. Blending Mode is a 22-item popup: 1 = None (default, gradient replaces the layer; a render at Opacity 60 showed a dimmed gradient over black with no footage). 2 = Normal is render-confirmed (Opacity 60 gives a four-colour wash with the footage visible underneath); the rest are in enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0) with separators at 3, 10, 13 and 18; only 1 and 2 have been rendered. Usually applied to a solid for a plate or to an adjustment layer for a wash.

verified.note: With Blending Mode 2 (Normal) at Opacity 60 the footage now stays visible under an orange/yellow/cyan/purple four-corner wash, where the old Mode 1 render was a dimmed gradient over black with the footage gone.

cards.name: Advanced Lightning
cards.summary: Draws a procedural electric lightning bolt with a bright core and coloured glow from an Origin towards a target or direction. Animating Conductivity State makes it flicker and re-branch.
use_for: trailer/hype moment: electricity crackling between two titles or graphic elements (a 'clash' beat)
power-sector or electricity explainer visuals
energy hit on a title slam in reels
storm ambience in a dramatic documentary reconstruction
avoid: leaving it static: a frozen bolt looks fake, animate Conductivity State
bolts drawn over real people's faces in news content can read as mockery; keep it on graphics
high Complexity with a large Glow Radius renders slowly

params.name: Lightning Type
params.does: 1-based popup: 1 Direction, 2 Strike, 3 Breaking, 4 Bouncey, 5 a separator, 6 Omni, 7 Anywhere, 8 Vertical, 9 Two-Way Strike
params.typical: 2 (Strike) for a bolt hitting a target, 1 (Direction) for an aimed bolt

params.name: Origin
params.does: start point of the bolt in comp pixels
params.typical: [960, 40] top centre

params.name: Contextual Control
params.does: direction point or strike target; for Omni/Anywhere it sets the radius

params.name: Conductivity State
params.does: random-variation seed; animating it makes the bolt flicker
params.typical: keyframe 0 -> 20-30 per second

params.name: Core Radius
params.does: thickness of the white core in px

params.name: Glow Radius
params.does: size of the coloured glow around the core

params.name: Glow Color
params.does: colour of the glow
params.typical: #4FA8FF electric blue or #B04FFF violet

params.name: Composite on Original
params.does: 0 = bolt only (layer pixels dropped), 1 = bolt drawn over the layer
params.typical: 1 on footage; 0 on a black solid set to Add/Screen

cards.scripting: Composite on Original defaults to 0, which drops the layer's own pixels and shows only the bolt: either set it to 1 or apply to a black solid in Add/Screen mode. Origin and Contextual Control are comp pixels; what Contextual Control means depends on Lightning Type (its UI label changes per type, hence the generic harvested name). Checkbox-like props (Decay Main Core, Composite on Original, Main Core Collision Only) are 0/1. Alpha Obstacle makes bolts avoid (+) or cling to (-) the layer's alpha edges. Lightning Type (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Direction, 2 Strike, 3 Breaking, 4 Bouncey, 5 a separator, 6 Omni, 7 Anywhere, 8 Vertical, 9 Two-Way Strike. Premiere's 'Lightning' is the older, simpler AE Lightning effect (different properties: Start point, End point, Segments ...), not this one.

verified.note: A bright white-core bolt with a light-blue glow strikes from the top centre down to the bottom through the centre of the frame, drawn over the footage.

cards.name: Audio Spectrum
cards.summary: Draws a frequency-spectrum visualiser (bars, lines or dots) from an audio layer along a straight line or a mask path (a circular mask gives a ring), moving with the music or voice.
use_for: podcast or interview clip audiograms for reels
visual bed under a voice-over-only explainer segment
music-reactive bars on a lyric or hype reel
circular spectrum ring around a speaker's photo
avoid: without an Audio Layer set it draws nothing
many thin bands flicker and shimmer after Instagram compression
the default magenta colours look like a stock template

params.name: Audio Layer
params.does: the layer whose audio drives the spectrum
params.typical: the VO or music layer index

params.name: Start Point
params.does: start of the baseline in comp pixels

params.name: End Point
params.does: end of the baseline in comp pixels

params.name: Frequency bands
params.does: number of bars/samples across the spectrum

params.name: End Frequency
params.does: highest frequency shown (Start Frequency is the lowest); content above it is not drawn
params.typical: 2000 default; 4000-8000 so speech sibilance and music highs also move the bars

params.name: Maximum Height
params.does: height scale of the bars in px

params.name: Thickness
params.does: width of each bar or line

params.name: Display Options
params.does: 1-based popup: Digital bars, Analog lines or Analog dots
params.typical: 1 (Digital) for clean bars

params.name: Inside Color
params.does: core colour of the bars (Outside Color is the soft edge)
params.typical: #FFFFFF with an Outside Color in the brand hue

cards.scripting: Audio Layer is a layer-type property and Path is a mask-type property: specs cannot set either. Use ExtendScript: eff.property("Audio Layer").setValue(audioLayer.index); eff.property("Path").setValue(maskIndex) for a mask on the same layer (0 = none, then Start/End Point are used). For a ring, draw a circular mask on the layer and pick it as Path (keep Use Polar Path 0); Use Polar Path 1 instead radiates the spectrum outward from Start Point as a starburst. Apply to a full-frame solid; Composite On Original 0 (default) shows only the visualiser. Hue Interpolation has no harvested range. Premiere has no built-in equivalent.

verified.note: status needs_input: needs an Audio Layer set by script, so no frame was made

cards.name: Audio Waveform
cards.summary: Draws the amplitude waveform of an audio layer as a moving line, bars or dots along a straight line or mask path, reacting to speech or music.
use_for: voice-reactive line under a podcast or talking-head clip
audiogram for quote clips from speeches in news reels
phone-call or leaked-audio style graphic in explainers
oscilloscope look for tech/AI content
avoid: without an Audio Layer set it draws nothing
a very short Audio Duration with high Maximum Height jitters wildly
default magenta colours look like a template

params.name: Audio Layer
params.does: the layer whose audio drives the waveform
params.typical: the VO or interview layer index

params.name: Start Point
params.does: start of the line in comp pixels

params.name: End Point
params.does: end of the line in comp pixels

params.name: Displayed Samples
params.does: number of points along the line; fewer = chunkier

params.name: Maximum Height
params.does: amplitude scale in px

params.name: Audio Duration (milliseconds)
params.does: time window of audio shown along the line

params.name: Thickness
params.does: line thickness

params.name: Display Options
params.does: 1-based popup: Digital, Analog lines or Analog dots
params.typical: 2 (Analog lines, default)

cards.scripting: Audio Layer is a layer-type property and Path is a mask-type property: specs cannot set either. Use ExtendScript: eff.property("Audio Layer").setValue(audioLayer.index); eff.property("Path").setValue(maskIndex) for a mask on the same layer (0 = none). Apply to a full-frame solid; Composite On Original 0 (default) shows only the waveform. Random Seed (Analog) only affects the Analog display styles. Premiere has no built-in equivalent.

verified.note: status needs_input: needs an Audio Layer set by script, so no frame was made

cards.name: Beam
cards.summary: Draws a glowing laser/light beam between a start and an end point. Animating Time sends a bolt of light travelling along the line.
use_for: animated glowing connector between two points on a map or diagram in an explainer
laser-scan reveal across a title in a tech/AI reel
light-streak element in trailer transitions
highlight line under a key statistic
avoid: the default pink/red colours look dated
Composite On Original 0 hides the layer: use a solid in Add/Screen or set it to 1
very thick beams with 3D Perspective look like cheap 90s lasers

params.name: Starting Point
params.does: start of the beam path in comp pixels
params.typical: any pixel point, often linked to a null

params.name: Ending Point
params.does: end of the beam path in comp pixels
params.typical: any pixel point

params.name: Length
params.does: beam length as a fraction of the start-to-end distance
params.typical: 0.2-1 (1 with Time 0.5 fills the whole line)

params.name: Time
params.does: how far the beam has travelled along the path (0.5 = centred)
params.typical: 0.5 for a static beam; animate 0 -> 1 to shoot it across

params.name: Starting Thickness
params.does: beam thickness at the start in px (Ending Thickness for the end)

params.name: Softness
params.does: edge falloff of the beam

params.name: Inside Color
params.does: hot core colour
params.typical: #FFFFFF

params.name: Outside Color
params.does: glow/edge colour
params.typical: #00C8FF cyan or a brand hue

cards.scripting: Length and Time are 0-1 fractions (the UI shows percent). Points are comp pixels; link them to Point Control or null positions with expressions for map connectors. 3D Perspective (0/1, default 1) scales thickness with depth. Composite On Original defaults to 0, which shows only the beam.

verified.note: A crisp cyan beam with a white core runs diagonally from lower left to upper right across the centre of the photo, footage intact.

cards.name: CC Glue Gun
cards.summary: Paints a glossy, wet-looking 3D-shaded bead of 'glue' along the path of an animated Brush Position, lit and reflecting the layer. With a static position it draws a single shiny blob.
use_for: playful liquid underline or write-on in an AI-tool or education reel
comic emphasis circle drawn around an object (animate Brush Position)
quirky glossy stroke for a social transition
avoid: looks gimmicky in serious news or political content
a static Brush Position only draws one blob; a stroke needs keyframes or an expression
large Wobble values make the bead lumpy and messy
it outputs only the bead: the rest of the layer turns transparent (black in an empty comp), so apply it to a duplicate above the footage

params.name: Brush Position
params.does: where the bead is laid down; its motion path becomes the stroke
params.typical: keyframed path in comp pixels

params.name: Stroke Width
params.does: bead thickness; not literal px (160 rendered a ~1000 px wide blob in a 1920 comp)
params.typical: 4 (default) to 20 for a stroke, roughly 25-125 px if the ~6x scale seen at 160 holds; 100+ for one big lens-like blob

params.name: Density
params.does: how closely blobs are packed along the stroke

params.name: Time Span (sec)
params.does: how much of the brush's past path stays visible
params.typical: 1-5 for a trailing stroke (behaviour at 0 not verified)

params.name: Reflection
params.does: how strongly the layer image reflects in the bead

params.name: Wobble Width
params.does: random sideways wobble of the bead

params.name: Light Intensity
params.does: brightness of the effect light on the bead

cards.scripting: Brush Position must be keyframed (or driven by an expression, e.g. a Point Control or wiggle) to draw a stroke; the bead accumulates along the brush's past path, so the demo still only shows one blob. Time Span (sec) limits how much history stays; its exact behaviour at the default 0 is not verified, so the demo sets 10 (longer than any test clip) to be safe either way. Using 2 needs a light layer in the comp. Light Direction has no harvested range (degrees). Paint Style: 1 Plain, 2 Wobbly; Using: 1 Effect Light, 2 AE Lights; Light Type: 1 Distant Light, 2 Point Light (read from After Effects 26.0). Low confidence overall: render a test before relying on it.

verified.note: A single large glossy sphere-like blob refracts the photo like a fisheye while everything outside it goes black (layer dropped); card now notes that.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: Stroke Width typical lowered from 20-80 to 4-20; frame 094 shows 160 gives a ~1000 px blob (about 6x), so 20-80 would be a 125-500 px bead, not a stroke

cards.name: CC Light Burst 2.5
cards.summary: Streaks the layer's own bright areas outward from a centre point into radial light rays, like a burst of volumetric light or a zoom-streak flash.
use_for: flash/light-burst transition between shots in trailers and hype reels
god rays behind a logo or title reveal
dramatic emphasis on a stage or podium moment in rally edits
energetic accent on a music beat in reels
avoid: on faces it smears features into streaks
high Intensity on full-frame footage clips the highlights to flat white
a full-strength burst held for seconds looks dated; keep it to a beat

params.name: Center
params.does: point the rays radiate from, in comp pixels
params.typical: on the brightest element, e.g. [960, 380]

params.name: Intensity
params.does: brightness/strength of the rays

params.name: Ray Length
params.does: length of the streaks; negative values pull inward

params.name: Burst
params.does: 1-based popup: ray style
params.typical: 2 (Fade, default)

params.name: Set Color
params.does: 0/1: tint the rays with Color
params.typical: 1 for a warm or brand-tinted burst

params.name: Color
params.does: ray tint when Set Color is 1
params.typical: #FFE640 warm gold

cards.scripting: Not a pure generator: rays come from the layer's own bright pixels, so dark footage shows little. Raise Intensity or apply it to a duplicated, brightened layer set to Add/Screen. Center is comp pixels. Halo Alpha and Set Color are 0/1 checkboxes. Burst: 1 Straight, 2 Fade (default), 3 Center (read from After Effects 26.0). For a flash, ramp Ray Length from 0 and keep Intensity at 100 at the ends: Intensity appears to scale the whole result's brightness (not verified), so keyframing it to 0 risks dark/black frames.

verified.note: Strong radial light streaks burst out from the upper centre, washing the frame bright and smearing the figures and stripes outward.
